Find the $x$-intercepts of the circle $(x-2)^{2}+(y-2)^{2}=20,$ shown above.
questions.worked_solution:
We must have $y=0$ at the $x$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+(y-2)^{2} & =20 \\ (x-2)^{2}+(0-2)^{2} & =20 \\ (x-2)^{2}+4 & =20 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =16 \\ x-2 & =\pm \sqrt{16} \\ x & =2\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-intercepts occur at the points $(-2,0)$ and $(6,0).$

When the circle intercepts the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$

So, we need to substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the circle and solve the resulting equation for $y$, if possible:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)^{2}+(y+2)^{2} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ (0+1)^{2}+(y+2)^{2} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ 1+(y+2)^{2} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ (y+2)^{2} & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the $y$-intercepts of the circle $x^2+y^2+2x-2y= 8,$ shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14275039/assets/8eb9a6488191e8cf8a5b6107f3501e7d01938cf071e77b75890d570fc99cbf7a.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
We must have $x = 0$ at the $y$-intercepts. 

So, we need to substitute $x = 0$ into the equation of the circle and solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+2x-2y & =8 \\ (0)^{2}+{y}^{2}+2(0)-2y & =8 \\ {y}^{2}-2y & =8\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this equation by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}-2y+1 & =8+1 \\ (y-1)^{2} & =9 \\ y-1 & =\pm 3 \\ y & =1\pm 3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $y$-intercepts occur at  $(0,-2)$ and $(0,4).$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
Consider the circle with equation 

$$
(x - 2)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 3^2,
$$

as shown below. How can we calculate the points where the circle intercepts the $x$-axis?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14275039/assets/6b80fa5fc106a8a78ba46e71ad8649da731a14777449b092f982e34138353b0a.png)

  

Remember, when the circle intercepts the $x$-axis, we must have $y = 0.$

Therefore, to find the $x$-intercepts of the circle, we need to set $y = 0$ in the equation of the circle and solve for $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)^{2}+(y-1)^{2} & ={3}^{2} \\ (x-2)^{2}+(0-1)^{2} & ={3}^{2} \\ (x-2)^{2}+1 & =9 \\ (x-2)^{2} & =8 \\ x-2 & =\pm \sqrt{8} \\ x-2 & =\pm 2\sqrt{2} \\ x & =2\pm 2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the circle intercepts the $x$-axis at $(2-2\sqrt{2},0)$ and $(2+2\sqrt{2},0).$
